open_pr_snapshot.command: gh pr list --repo TaoSama/vibe-screen --state open --limit 200 --json number,title,headRefName,headRefOid,baseRefName,updatedAt,isDraft,mergeStateStatus,url | jq 'map(select(.number != 737)) | sort_by(.number)'

merged_pr_snapshot.command: gh pr list --repo TaoSama/vibe-screen --state merged --base main --limit 250 --json number,title,mergedAt,headRefOid,baseRefName,mergeCommit,url --jq '.[] | select(.number>=568 and .number<=736)'

required_phrases: Do not treat roadmap items below as shipped features

required_gates.title: Protocol v1 contract and CI gates
Android tests and debug APK clean build
macOS release build and full-Xcode unit tests
macOS Host hardware compatibility matrix
blockers: The published current-base macos-hardware-compatibility-gate summaries for Mac16,8 readiness are blocked, not passing.

The aggregate now requires at least one formal macOS Host compatibility row with verdict pass, a retained same-bundle gate_input artifact, required artifact roles, and repository_commit matching this manifest base before this gate can close.

Read-only Screen Recording, Accessibility, and Microphone TCC rows are not proven for a stable signed Host whose csreq, TCC auth_reason, bundle id, install path, pinned signing leaf, canonical designated requirement, and source provenance satisfy the hardened current-source gate.
Full macOS checks, packaged runtime launch, Protocol v1 stream, input smoke, and reconnect evidence are missing for that row.
Intel Macs, additional Apple silicon models, macOS builds, and display topologies still require exact-row passing evidence before support claims.

PR #731 guards the macOS Host readiness login probe and documents opt-in current-user/login-item constraints, but this is read-only preflight hardening only and does not add a passing hardware compatibility matrix row.

required_gates.title: Android USB stream, reconnect, stale epoch, and codec fallback
Telemetry and external latency artifact archive
blockers: PR #557 adds Android stream telemetry counters for dropped frames, decoder latency, session epoch, wire mode, and heartbeat source with focused JVM coverage, but these counters are diagnostic/source readiness only. PR #656, PR #671, and PR #701 further harden the formal latency/telemetry archive validators so malformed, insufficient, non-revalidating, or textually non-closing latency packages fail closed; this is evidence-tool hardening only. PR #706 hardens Host RSS readiness safety checks only, PR #707 clarifies macOS compatibility TCC documentation/source-guard behavior only, and neither adds external latency closure evidence.

The tightened current-base latency gate remains blocked readiness; no external-camera latency sample package, raw camera media, annotated sample set, or synchronized-clock physical-input proof exists for the Phase 0 evidence archive.

required_gates.title: Host RSS two-hour no-growth gate
blockers: The retained two-hour Xiaomi 13 stream was stable but Host RSS grew about 18.3 MB with a positive second-half slope.
No current-source host_rss_gate pass exists.

The latest current-base readiness records are blocked before a stable-signed, read-only TCC-proven, listener-observed current-source Host can be launched with native VIBE_SCREEN_TELEMETRY_PATH coverage and a USB/LAN stream window.

PR #706 hardens Host RSS readiness safety metadata validation so readiness packages that install or replace the Host, claim to close runtime gates, or omit required structured source paths fail closed; PR #707 only clarifies macOS compatibility TCC documentation/source-guard behavior. These changes do not provide a current-source two-hour no-growth pass.

required_gates.title: Native pointer HID mouse move/click acceptance
blockers: No physical Android mouse, touchpad, or trackball was attached during a Protocol v1 run.
PR #558 adds Android native pointer hover enter/exit mapping and fail-closed unsupported-button filtering with focused JVM coverage, but this is source/unit readiness only.

The latest current-base native-pointer HID summaries remain blocked and do not retain Android forwarding logs, Host pointer-injection logs, and visible Mac move/click result from the same observation window.

PR #727 hardens native-pointer HID retained report validation by requiring observation artifacts for Android forwarding, Host injection, and visible Mac result; this is evidence-tool hardening only and does not add a physical HID pointer pass.

required_gates.title: Controller runtime acceptance
blockers: No physical Android controller runtime run is recorded.
No identity-signed Host with approved virtual HID entitlement, Host availability, Mac-side response, and neutral release on disconnect is recorded in one pass evidence bundle.

required_gates.title: Android/macOS clipboard product E2E
blockers: Host readiness is blocked on stable signing, installed Host source provenance, read-only Screen Recording, Accessibility, and Microphone TCC verification, Host listener availability, virtual HID entitlement, and login/headless readiness.

Android now requires explicit overwrite confirmation, pending-action status visibility, duplicate action suppression, PR #620 allowed-state managed-policy control happy-path coverage, and control-boundary coverage before writing solicited or direct Mac clipboard content into ClipboardManager, but this is source/contract and local Android readiness rather than system-pasteboard product E2E. PR #659 improves Android clipboard confirmation dialog source behavior, but does not add retained Android ClipboardManager <-> macOS NSPasteboard product evidence.

No retained bidirectional Android ClipboardManager -> macOS NSPasteboard and macOS NSPasteboard -> Android ClipboardManager product transfer evidence exists with exact system clipboard endpoints, explicit user action, Protocol v1 session ownership, verified session epoch, verified origin device ID, 16-byte change ID, SHA-256 digest, bounded byte length, final digest match, distinct markers, final marker equality, and evidence-relative non-empty retained artifacts for source read, sender action, receiver approval, protocol packets, destination write, final verification, and negative boundary verification, with each role backed by a distinct file whose declared direction, recorded byte length, and SHA-256 match the retained bytes, whose destination-write artifact matches the direction-level payload size and digest, and whose protocol-packet JSONL contains offer/request/content records matching the transfer direction, change ID, session epoch, and origin.

Existing P0110 evidence proves only local Android ClipboardManager smoke and offline/protocol readiness; the 2026-09-08 current-main no-Host refresh expands ClipboardManagerInstrumentedTest to 8 executed tests for ordinary foreground text, instrumentation set/read, 256 KiB and 320 KiB UTF-8 text, empty clipboard clearing, non-text Intent ClipData, and multi-item first-non-text handling, plus 2 clipboard confirmation dialog layout tests. Exploratory 512 KiB and 1 MiB local Android system-clipboard writes hit Binder transaction-size limits on P0110, so the Protocol v1 1 MiB ceiling remains JVM/protocol evidence only. This no-Host smoke must not be relabeled as Xiaomi 13/fuxi evidence and cannot close Android/macOS system-pasteboard product E2E.

PR #726 hardens clipboard product E2E artifact validation for direction-scoped payload metadata and retained bytes; this is evidence-tool hardening only and does not add Android ClipboardManager <-> macOS NSPasteboard product evidence.
PR #735 records P0110 no-Host UI/UX evidence for clipboard confirmation layout/control surfaces only; it does not add Android ClipboardManager <-> macOS NSPasteboard product evidence.

required_gates.title: Android/macOS file-transfer product E2E
blockers: Android PR #551/#552/#553 and PR #560/#561 add no-Host readiness, outgoing progress, control reachability, and progress-state race hardening, but these are source/contract readiness rather than retained Host-backed bidirectional product transfer evidence.
Android now exposes incoming file-transfer progress and user cancellation in source and contract tests, but this is not a retained Host-backed bidirectional product transfer pass.
Host readiness is blocked on stable signing, source provenance, read-only Screen Recording, Accessibility, and Microphone TCC verification, virtual HID entitlement, and login/headless readiness.

No retained bidirectional Android -> macOS and macOS -> Android product transfer evidence exists with file offer/request/content packets, explicit sender action, receiver approval, remote write, verified session ID and session epoch, distinct 16-byte transfer IDs, distinct file names and SHA-256 payload digests, observed progress, exact source/destination file endpoints, evidence-relative non-empty artifacts with distinct files per role, and cancel cleanup.

PR #555 and PR #562 record P0110 no-Host transfer UI smoke only; they do not prove real Host readiness, stream establishment, Protocol v1 handshake with a real Host, or Android/macOS file bytes landing behavior.
PR #563 keeps active outgoing transfer controls visible while sending and resets disconnected transfer controls with Android source-level contract coverage only.

PR #564 treats Internet outgoing file-transfer cancellation as locally successful after local owner cleanup and retains fail-closed session behavior when the reliable cancel frame is rejected, but this is Internet semantic offline coverage only.

PR #567 shows accepted incoming file-transfer progress in the Android control bar, adds incoming cancellation cleanup, and keeps incoming/outgoing transfer workflows mutually exclusive with source-level contract coverage only.

PR #590, PR #597, PR #609, PR #612, PR #615, PR #616, and PR #619 add transfer-progress layout, no-Host boundary, runtime-loss, settings-heading, selectable guidance, and app-specific local-save cleanup coverage, but all remain source/unit/no-Host readiness.

PR #653 adds Nubia P0110/pacific no-Host Internet secondary-action large-text and narrow-screen UI/UX evidence, but it is not Host-backed file-transfer product E2E evidence and does not prove bytes landing on macOS or Android.

PR #657 improves incoming file-offer readability, PR #659 improves clipboard confirmation dialogs, PR #660 adds outgoing file-transfer confirmation, PR #658 shows audio readiness in Settings, PR #663 hardens required file-transfer artifact role validation, PR #664 rejects reused clipboard retained artifacts, PR #665 and PR #670 harden the file-transfer smoke evidence gate against zero-test, unrelated-summary, or summary-only evidence, PR #668 verifies remote file-transfer artifact coverage, and PR #666 adds current-main no-Host dialog layout evidence for clipboard confirmations and file-transfer offer/preflight dialogs; these are source/UI/readiness or evidence-tool updates only and do not prove Host-backed file-transfer bytes landing.

PR #726 hardens file-transfer product E2E artifact validation for direction-scoped payload metadata, destination-write size/digest matching, and retained bytes; this is evidence-tool hardening only and does not prove Host-backed file-transfer bytes landing. PR #732 hardens file-transfer cleanup-state evidence validation only and likewise does not add Host-backed file-transfer bytes landing.

PR #736 hardens aggregate file-transfer product E2E revalidation so Android->macOS and macOS->Android evidence must each carry a valid 32-character hex session_id_hex and both directions must share that same session_id_hex before the source.product_e2e record can close; this is fail-closed evidence-tool hardening only and does not add Host-backed file-transfer product bytes landing evidence.

The file-transfer/WebRTC bulk current-base aggregate remains fail-closed until both the Android USB/LAN file-transfer child gate and public Internet WebRTC bulk product-flow child gate independently pass.
PR #735 records P0110 no-Host UI/UX evidence for file-transfer offer/preflight/control surfaces only; it does not add Host-backed file-transfer product bytes landing evidence.
